newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shanghai seen testbed for telecoms deregulation.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai seen testbed for telecoms deregulation.

text.p: China is expected to pass national telecommunications rules by the year 2000, the chief of AT&T Corp's China unit said on Wednesday.

"I am confident that some time in this five-year plan (1996-2000), the national telecom law will be passed," William Warwick, chairman and chief executive at AT&T (China) Co Ltd, told reporters after a business seminar.
The country, which bans foreign ownership or operation or telecommunications services, might experiment by partially opening up the business to foreign players in a Shanghai district, he said.

"China will probably in some way experiment, maybe in Pudong, with a foreign company as the partner in providing services in a joint venture with a Chinese telephone company and maybe the local government. But this kind of structure will still comply with the Chinese requirement that the foreign partner does not own or operate directly the network," he said.
Warwick said AT&T was among a number of foreign companies discussing with Chinese authorities over a telecommunications project in Pudong district in Shanghai, he said.
"China is definitely opening its doors in terms of technology and it is installing the latest technology in the world, truly in terms of equipment technology," Warwick said.
"It will be the second largest network in the world in the year 2000 and it will obviously quickly surpass the United States network after that time," he said.
The official projection of 18 million mobile phone subscribers by the year 2000 was understated, he said. The figure could be as high as 30 million.
Lucent Technologies Inc, a spin-off of AT&T, was negotiating a joint venture deal in China to make CDMA (code division multiple access) equipment, Warwick said.
